predictions.explanation:
Evidence from U.S. surveillance data shows that both components of Friedberg’s prediction came true.

1. **Deaths rose substantially after late July 2021.**  In CDC’s Weekly Review for the week of July 21, 2021 (published July 23), the U.S. 7‑day moving average of new COVID‑19 deaths was **223 per day**.  �citeturn6search0 By late September 2021, during the Delta surge, CDC reported a **7‑day average of 1,476 deaths per day** (week of September 29), more than a six‑fold increase from July levels.  �citeturn6search5 This matches his claim that deaths would rise from the then‑current baseline.

2. **The increase was driven primarily by unvaccinated people.**  A CDC analysis of 13 jurisdictions for April 4–July 17, 2021 (i.e., leading right up to this podcast) found that **91% of COVID‑19 deaths** in that period occurred among people who were *not fully vaccinated*, with only 9% among fully vaccinated individuals.  �citeturn7search0  A Peterson‑KFF analysis using CDC data from 25 jurisdictions estimated that from **June 2021 through March 2022**, about **270,000 of 389,000 adult COVID deaths (≈69%)** occurred in unvaccinated adults, and that 86% of adult deaths in June 2021 and still 60% in early 2022 were among the unvaccinated.  �citeturn9view0  Separate KFF/Epic work similarly found that from June–September 2021, **around 85% of COVID hospitalizations** were in people not fully vaccinated, with CDC data implying roughly 95–99% of early‑summer 2021 hospital admissions were among the unvaccinated.  �citeturn0search0turn0search1  These data show that as deaths climbed during the Delta wave after July 2021, the **“bulk” of those severe outcomes were indeed in the unvaccinated**, as Friedberg predicted.

Given that both (a) deaths clearly rose from late‑July levels and (b) the surge was overwhelmingly concentrated in unvaccinated people, this prediction is best classified as **right**.
predictions.grok_explanation: US COVID-19 deaths increased after July 2021 due to the Delta wave. Weekly deaths rose from ~2,000-3,000 in late July to peaks of ~13,000-15,000 in September 2021 (CDC Provisional Death Counts: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr/covid_weekly/index.htm; Our World in Data COVID deaths tracker). This increase was primarily among unvaccinated people, who accounted for the bulk of deaths: e.g., ~74% of deaths Oct-Dec 2021 (Delta period) were unvaccinated vs. 26% vaccinated (CDC MMWR: https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/72/wr/mm7206a3.htm); unvaccinated death rates 16x higher than vaccinated (RR=16.2). Earlier Delta data shows similar disparities, with nearly all August 2021 deaths among unvaccinated (KFF/Health System Tracker: https://www.healthsystemtracker.org/brief/covid-19-continues-to-be-a-leading-cause-of-death-in-the-u-s-in-august-2021/). CDC confirmed unvaccinated had 53x higher death risk in periods following (CDC MMWR vol.71: https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/71/wr/mm7104e2.htm).

predictions.explanation:
Based on evidence up to **November 29, 2025**, no SARS‑CoV‑2 variant has matched the combination of outcomes Chamath described:

1. **"Overcome all the vaccines we have"**  
   - Variants like **Delta** and especially **Omicron** and its sublineages have shown **immune escape**, reducing protection against infection and mild disease. However, updated vaccines (bivalent and later XBB‑targeting, then JN.1‑/KP.2‑adapted) have continued to provide substantial protection against **severe disease, hospitalization, and death**, especially in boosted and high‑risk groups, rather than being completely “overcome.” 

2. **"Kill enormous numbers of people, including the vaccinated"**  
   - COVID‑19 has caused very large global mortality overall, but after mass vaccination, excess mortality and death rates have been **disproportionately concentrated among the unvaccinated, under‑vaccinated, and the very old / clinically vulnerable**, not “enormous numbers” of otherwise‑typical vaccinated people. No post‑vaccine variant has had mortality anywhere near what this quote implies among vaccinated populations.

3. **"Will literally shut the economy down"**  
   - Since mid‑2021, there **have not** been renewed shutdowns of the global or U.S. economy comparable to the broad stay‑at‑home orders and mandated closures of early 2020. There have been **localized or sector‑specific disruptions** and short‑term restrictions in some countries during waves (e.g., late Delta, early Omicron, and some later surges), but economic activity overall has **remained open**, with most countries moving to mitigation and living‑with‑COVID strategies.

Because by late 2025:
- No variant has fully **defeated all available vaccines** in preventing severe disease,
- No variant has caused **catastrophic mortality among vaccinated people**, and
- There has been **no return to 2020‑style comprehensive economic shutdowns**,

the specific compound prediction as stated is **wrong** rather than merely "too early" or "ambiguous."
predictions.grok_explanation: No COVID-19 variant post-July 2021 substantially evaded vaccines to cause **very high mortality including among vaccinated** people or force renewed economy-wide shutdowns. Omicron and subvariants (e.g., XBB, NB.1.8.1, XFG in 2025) showed immune evasion for *infections* but vaccines/boosters retained strong protection against severe outcomes/deaths (e.g., [NEJM Oct 2025](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2510226): 2024-2025 vaccine reduced deaths by ~2.2 per 100k; [Our World in Data](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/united-states-rates-of-covid-19-deaths-by-vaccination-status): consistently lower death rates in vaccinated). Global/US lockdowns ended by 2022-2023 ([Wikipedia COVID lockdowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_lockdowns), [CDC timeline](https://www.cdc.gov/museum/timeline/covid19.html)); no renewed shutdowns despite surges ([Reuters Mar 2025](https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/five-years-economic-impact-covid-19-lingers-2025-03-08/)). Mortality declined sharply post-vaccination/immunity; no 'enormous numbers of deaths' forcing economic halt.

predictions.explanation:
Evidence since 2021 supports Friedberg’s forecast that COVID-19 would become and remain an endemic virus with ongoing outbreaks, despite extensive infection and vaccination.

* By August 2024, U.S. health officials (CDC) publicly described COVID-19 as **endemic throughout the world**, emphasizing it is “here to stay” and will continue to circulate and cause illness indefinitely, managed alongside other endemic diseases rather than as a unique pandemic threat.
  ([kuaf.com](https://www.kuaf.com/npr-news/2024-08-09/is-covid-endemic-yet-yep-says-the-cdc-heres-what-that-means?utm_source=openai))
* CDC guidance in 2024 notes that COVID-19 **surges throughout the year**, with peaks in winter and additional surges in other seasons driven by new variants and waning immunity—i.e., ongoing intermittent modest-to-severe outbreaks rather than elimination. ([restoredcdc.org](https://restoredcdc.org/www.cdc.gov/ncird/whats-new/covid-19-can-surge-throughout-the-year.html?utm_source=openai))
* A March 2025 analysis reports that five years after the pandemic began, experts consider COVID-19 to have **transitioned into an endemic phase**, still highly transmissible and capable of severe outbreaks, even though annual deaths and hospitalizations have declined. ([washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/wellness/2025/03/13/covid-endemic-pandemic-five-years/?utm_source=openai))
* That same reporting notes that over **80% of U.S. adults have received at least one COVID vaccine dose**, yet the virus continues to circulate and cause significant morbidity and mortality, confirming the prediction that circulation would persist “no matter how many people get it [or] get vaccinated.” ([washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/wellness/2025/03/13/covid-endemic-pandemic-five-years/?utm_source=openai))
* Reviews of SARS‑CoV‑2 epidemiology since 2022 explicitly describe or project a **transition to endemicity**, with the virus expected to become a long-term, seasonal/endemic human coronavirus rather than being eradicated. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic?utm_source=openai))
* Expert commentary in 2024 characterizes the situation as **“endemic but with periodic epidemics,”** directly matching the idea of ongoing intermittent outbreaks over many years. ([opb.org](https://www.opb.org/article/2024/08/09/is-covid-endemic-yet-yep-says-the-cdc-here-s-what-that-means/?utm_source=openai))

By late 2025, COVID-19 is widely regarded as an endemic virus that continues to circulate globally with periodic surges, despite widespread prior infection and vaccination. This aligns closely with Friedberg’s 2021 prediction, so it is best judged **right**.

predictions.explanation:
Evidence shows that DeepMind did exactly what Friedberg described.

* **Scale (>100M proteins from many species):**
  * The AlphaFold Protein Structure Database (AFDB) launched in July 2021 with ~350k structures for humans and 20 model organisms. ([deepmind.google](https://deepmind.google/science/alphafold/?utm_source=openai))
  * On **28 July 2022**, DeepMind and EMBL‑EBI expanded AFDB to **over 200 million predicted protein structures** covering almost the whole UniProt/“nearly all catalogued proteins known to science,” including plants, bacteria, animals, and other organisms — far above the 100M threshold and clearly spanning many species. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/news/science/alphafold-200-million/?utm_source=openai))
  * Later summaries and analyses confirm that AFDB now contains **over 214 million** predicted structures. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37704730/?utm_source=openai))

* **Freely available and searchable:**
  * DeepMind and EMBL‑EBI explicitly describe the expanded AlphaFold database as **freely and openly available** to the scientific community. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/news/science/alphafold-200-million/?utm_source=openai))
  * EMBL‑EBI’s Job Dispatcher blog notes that the AFDB dataset is available for **sequence searching** in their similarity-search tools and via Dbfetch, and a 2024 NAR paper details expanded search and filtering capabilities, confirming that the database is actively **searchable**. ([ebi.ac.uk](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/jdispatcher/blog/2022-07-28-new-afdb-release?utm_source=openai))

* **Timing (“over the coming months” after July 2021):**
  * Friedberg spoke in July 2021, citing DeepMind’s plan to scale to >100M proteins "over the coming months." The AFDB’s massive expansion to >200M structures occurred on **28 July 2022**, about one year later. ([deepmind.google](https://deepmind.google/science/alphafold/?utm_source=openai))
  * The foundational Nucleic Acids Research paper itself used the same language, stating that **“in the coming months”** the database would be expanded to cover over 130M UniRef90 cluster representatives, i.e., >100M proteins, which is what was then realized by the 2022 expansion. ([academic.oup.com](https://academic.oup.com/nar/article-abstract/50/D1/D439/6430488?utm_source=openai))

Given that (1) the database did expand beyond 100M proteins, (2) they are from many species, (3) the data are freely available and searchable, and (4) this major expansion occurred roughly a year after the July 2021 prediction—consistent with the loose “coming months” phrasing—Friedberg’s prediction is best classified as **right**.

predictions.grok_explanation: The AlphaFold Protein Structure Database launched on July 22, 2021, with ~365,000 predicted structures from 21 model organisms, including humans ([EMBL press release](https://www.embl.org/news/science/alphafold-database-launch/), [DeepMind](https://deepmind.google/science/alphafold/)). DeepMind announced plans to expand to over 100 million structures 'in the coming months' ([MIT Technology Review, July 22, 2021](https://www.technologyreview.com/2021/07/22/1029973/deepmind-alphafold-protein-folding-biology-disease-drugs-proteome/)). However, the database grew gradually to nearly 1 million structures before the major expansion to over 200 million on July 28, 2022, covering nearly all catalogued proteins in UniProt from many species ([EMBL announcement](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/about/news/technology-and-innovation/alphafold-200-million), [DeepMind blog, July 22, 2022](https://deepmind.google/blog/putting-the-power-of-alphafold-into-the-worlds-hands/)). No evidence of reaching over 100 million unique structures within months (e.g., by late 2021). The database is freely available and searchable ([AlphaFold DB](https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/)), but the timeline failed. ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AlphaFold), [NAR paper, 2022](https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/50/D1/D439/6430488)).

predictions.explanation:
Available evidence shows AlphaFold and its protein-structure database (launched July 22, 2021) have been widely adopted and clearly inspired some new therapeutics-focused companies, but there is no reliable count tying **hundreds** of new drug companies specifically to that database.

Key points:

* The AlphaFold Protein Structure Database was released in July 2021 and rapidly expanded to >200 million predicted protein structures, covering almost all known proteins.([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AlphaFold?utm_source=openai))  It has since been used by millions of researchers in over 190 countries and has become a routine tool in disease-focused research and early drug discovery.([sciencebusiness.net](https://sciencebusiness.net/network-updates/embl-ebi-and-google-deepmind-renew-partnership-and-release-update-alphafold?utm_source=openai))  This supports the idea that it is an important enabling technology for therapeutics.

* Multiple new drug discovery startups explicitly build on AlphaFold or its ideas. Isomorphic Labs (founded 2021 as a DeepMind/Alphabet spin‑out) describes its founding as **built on AlphaFold** and uses AlphaFold models centrally in its AI drug-design engine.([startupsweek.com](https://startupsweek.com/2025/04/02/google-deepmind-ceos-startup-raises-600-million/?utm_source=openai))  Latent Labs, founded in 2025 by a former AlphaFold2 scientist, likewise aims to use AI and protein-structure knowledge to design synthetic therapeutic proteins.([ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/92143d49-c777-4bba-8857-b4ef7e82ebd4?utm_source=openai))  A Guardian analysis notes "companies built on AlphaFold" and highlights AlphaProteo using AlphaFold’s structures to design drug-like molecules.([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/ng-interactive/2025/mar/28/ai-alphafold-biology-protein-structure?utm_source=openai))  These examples confirm that **some** therapeutics-focused companies have indeed started around this resource.

* However, industry mapping of "AI in drug discovery" shows a broad ecosystem. A 2025 BiopharmaTrend report tracks **500+ AI-related startups in pharma/biotech**, but many of these are not de novo drug-discovery companies (they may focus on clinical trials, repurposing, disease modeling, or software tools).([biopharmatrend.com](https://www.biopharmatrend.com/ai-drug-discovery-pipeline/?utm_source=openai))  Public surveys and market reports categorize companies by use of AI, not by whether they **rely materially on the AlphaFold database** or were *founded because* the database became available.

* None of the major surveys, consulting reports, or news overviews found provide a breakdown such as "number of post‑2021 drug-discovery startups whose core platform depends on AlphaFold/its database", nor even a rough "hundreds of AlphaFold‑based startups" figure. They typically discuss AlphaFold as a widely used tool, mention a handful of emblematic startups, and then describe a much larger AI‑drug‑discovery sector without linking company formation counts causally to AlphaFold.

Given this, we can confidently say that **some** new therapeutics-focused companies were founded around AlphaFold and its database, and that its impact on the ecosystem is substantial. But we **cannot** empirically verify that "hundreds" of such companies have been founded *because of* that database, nor can we rule it out using available data. The causal, quantitative claim in the prediction therefore cannot be determined from current evidence, even though enough time has passed since 2021 to observe many company launches. Hence the outcome is best classified as **ambiguous** rather than clearly right or wrong.

predictions.explanation:
By late 2025, the large tech platforms remain highly centralized and dominant. Google still handles roughly 89–91% of global search queries across devices, while Bing and other competitors remain in low single digits, indicating only small erosions of its dominance rather than a structural decentralization of the market.citeturn0search2turn0search5 Amazon continues to control around 37–38% of U.S. e‑commerce—an order of magnitude larger than its nearest rivals—showing persistent concentration in online retail.citeturn0search6turn0search7

There *has* been movement on the legislative and regulatory front that points in the direction Chamath described. The EU’s Digital Markets Act formally designates Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, and others as “gatekeepers” and imposes interoperability and self‑preferencing limits meant to open up competition.citeturn0search0 In the U.S., the Department of Justice has won major antitrust decisions against Google in both search and ad tech, with courts finding it violated Section 2 of the Sherman Act, though remedies and appeals are still ongoing and no breakup or equivalent structural remedy has yet occurred.citeturn0search18turn0search20

Meanwhile, the business reality is that the biggest platforms have become *more* valuable; Alphabet is close to a $4 trillion valuation and is described in financial press as a “monument to monopoly power,” underscoring that market structure remains highly centralized even amidst AI‑driven competition.citeturn0news16

Since Chamath framed this as a **“long run”** prediction without a concrete time horizon, and the legal/technological shifts that might decentralize these markets are still in early or unresolved stages, it’s too early to say whether we *ultimately* end up in a “materially healthier” and more decentralized structure than in 2021. On current evidence, the trend he describes has begun in policy and innovation terms but has not yet produced the structural outcome he forecast. Therefore the status as of November 2025 is **inconclusive (too early to tell)** rather than clearly right or wrong.
predictions.grok_explanation: As of December 2025, approximately 4.5 years after the July 2021 prediction, there has been no material shift from the centralized, monopolistic structure of major tech platforms like Google, Meta (Facebook), and Amazon to a more decentralized market. Google maintains ~90% global search market share ([Statcounter](https://gs.statcounter.com/search-engine-market-share)), Meta and Google dominate digital advertising (~50% combined, [Axios Oct 2025](https://www.axios.com/2025/10/18/google-meta-advertising)), and Facebook/YouTube lead U.S. social media usage ([Pew Nov 2025](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/survey-youtube-facebook-still-dominate-180007422.html)). Antitrust actions include U.S. rulings affirming Google's search monopoly with restraints but no breakup ([NYT Sep 2025](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/03/technology/google-ruling-antitrust.html)), ongoing ad tech cases, and EU DMA fines/enforcement against Apple/Meta/Google for compliance issues without fostering decentralization ([EC Apr 2025](https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_25_1085); [Bruegel May 2025](https://www.bruegel.org/newsletter/how-does-current-dma-enforcement-affect-digital-market-competition)). No evidence of innovation-driven decentralization (e.g., Web3/DeFi remains niche); AI power stays concentrated in Big Tech ([Pymnts Oct 2025](https://www.pymnts.com/artificial-intelligence-2/2025/decentralization-emerges-as-a-test-of-big-techs-ai-power/)). Competitive/societal outcomes not materially healthier, with dominance intact.

predictions.explanation:
Evidence from 2021–2025 shows that the privately led “space race” among SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Virgin Galactic has in fact produced major engineering advances and enabled new scientific work beyond the mid‑2021 state of the art.

**1. Clear engineering breakthroughs**
- **SpaceX Starship**: Since 2023, Starship—now the most powerful rocket ever built, powered by clusters of methane full‑flow staged‑combustion Raptor engines—has progressed from initial failures to a fully intact fourth test flight on June 6, 2024. That flight reached space, completed stage separation, survived re‑entry, and executed controlled splashdowns of both stages, a substantial leap beyond any capability that existed in mid‑2021. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/science/article/2024/jun/06/spacex-starship-successful-test-flight?utm_source=openai))  This is precisely the kind of large, reusable super‑heavy system Sacks was referring to.
- **Blue Origin New Glenn**: Blue Origin advanced from only suborbital New Shepard flights in 2021 to flying **New Glenn**, a heavy‑lift, partially reusable orbital rocket first launched in January 2025 and now with two successful missions. New Glenn can loft ~45 metric tons to LEO and has a reusable first stage designed for many re‑flights; the second mission in November 2025 both deployed NASA’s ESCAPADE Mars probes and achieved the first successful booster landing, a major new engineering capability for the company and for commercial launch options beyond what existed in 2021. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Glenn?utm_source=openai))
- **Deepening reusability across the sector**: These developments—Starship’s large fully reusable architecture and New Glenn’s heavy‑lift, barge‑landed first stage—go significantly beyond the mid‑2021 baseline of Falcon 9 / New Shepard / unproven Starship prototypes, and they are explicitly motivated by competitive commercial goals.

**2. Scientific and technological advances enabled by these systems**
- **Suborbital research (Virgin Galactic & Blue Origin)**: Virgin Galactic’s *Galactic 01* (June 2023), its first commercial flight, was a dedicated Italian Air Force research mission conducting 13 human‑tended and autonomous microgravity experiments in biomedical science, thermo‑fluid dynamics, and novel materials, all using the suborbital platform that didn’t exist in operational form in 2021. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galactic_01?utm_source=openai))  Subsequent flights like *Galactic 07* carried a mix of private astronauts and a national agency researcher, again using the vehicle as a microgravity lab. ([virgin.com](https://www.virgin.com/about-virgin/latest/virgin-galactic-completes-12th-successful-spaceflight?utm_source=openai))
- **Blue Origin New Shepard science missions**: New Shepard has evolved into a routine research platform: by 2025 it has flown over 175 scientific payloads above the Kármán line, including NASA‑sponsored technology tests such as precision lunar‑landing sensors and, notably in 2025, a flight that spun the capsule to simulate lunar gravity for about two minutes to test lunar‑surface technologies—something that previously required far more expensive facilities. ([blueorigin.com](https://www.blueorigin.com/news/new-shepard-ns-33-mission?utm_source=openai))
- **Mars science via commercial heavy lift (ESCAPADE)**: Blue Origin’s New Glenn has now launched NASA’s twin ESCAPADE orbiters, which will study Mars’ magnetic environment and atmospheric loss—science missions that, by design, ride on this new commercial, reusable heavy‑lift system rather than bespoke government rockets. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/4e3e6c380b8294b557618a6fea92282b?utm_source=openai))  While most of the scientific results will emerge after 2025, the missions themselves are a direct outcome of the private heavy‑lift race.

Given these concrete advances—large fully or partially reusable heavy‑lift systems that did not yet exist operationally in mid‑2021, and a growing stream of suborbital and interplanetary science enabled by them—the prediction that this new privately driven space race would produce “great engineering and scientific breakthroughs” in the following years has clearly been borne out.
